security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives involving Markdown syntax, normal Vaex memory mapping, and data-analysis terminology. Confirmed risks include public server binding, inline cloud credentials, and an unchecked file deletion example. Semantic review also found plaintext WebSocket guidance and an inline database password example; no prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Remote server examples expose data services without secure defaults.
remediation.suggestion: Bind to loopback by default, require authentication, use TLS, and explain firewall controls before allowing remote access.

remediation.issue: Cloud and database examples place credentials directly in source text.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables, credential providers, or secret managers, and avoid passwords inside connection strings.

remediation.issue: The archive example deletes the original file without verification.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the compressed output, request explicit confirmation, and keep the source until integrity checks succeed.

content.value_statement: Large tabular datasets can exceed memory and make standard DataFrame workflows slow or unreliable. This skill provides practical Vaex patterns for lazy analysis, visualization, conversion, and machine learning.
actual_capabilities: Open and create Vaex DataFrames from HDF5, Arrow, Parquet, CSV, pandas, NumPy, and dictionaries.
Build lazy filters, expressions, virtual columns, grouped aggregations, and multidimensional statistics.
Recommend memory-efficient formats, chunking, caching, delayed execution, and checkpoint strategies.
Create large-scale histograms, heatmaps, selection comparisons, subplots, and publication exports.
Assemble preprocessing and model workflows with Vaex, scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Keras.
Guide local, cloud, database, and Vaex Server data input and output.
limitations: Provides reference guidance and examples; it does not install Vaex or execute workflows automatically.
Requires access to user-provided datasets, paths, credentials, and compatible storage services.
API examples may depend on Vaex and integration library versions.
Large exports, sorting, or conversion to pandas can still require substantial disk space or memory.

use_cases.title: Convert Large Data Pipelines
use_cases.description: Plan efficient conversion from CSV or Parquet into HDF5 or Arrow with checkpoints and repeatable loading.

use_cases.title: Explore Billions of Rows
use_cases.description: Create lazy statistics, grouped summaries, filters, and visualizations without loading the full dataset into memory.

use_cases.title: Build Scalable Research Models
use_cases.description: Prepare features, train supported models, evaluate results, and preserve pipeline state for large scientific datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Large Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [file path] with Vaex. Show its schema, row count, missing-value summary, and five useful statistics without converting the full dataset to pandas.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Lazy Transformation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Vaex workflow for [dataset]. Filter by [condition], create [derived columns], group by [columns], and compute [metrics] while keeping operations lazy.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Data Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Vaex pipeline: [steps]. Identify memory and input-output bottlenecks, then propose batching, caching, materialization, checkpoint, and format improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Create an End-to-End ML Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Vaex machine learning workflow for [goal] using [features] and [target]. Include preprocessing, validation, model integration, state saving, and production inference.

output_examples.input: Summarize a 300 GB Parquet dataset by region and month.
output: Open the Parquet dataset with Vaex and inspect column types before aggregation.
Create a virtual month column from the timestamp field.
Group by region and month, then compute counts, totals, means, and missing values.
Export the compact summary to Arrow or Parquet.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow workflow that repeatedly calculates five statistics.
output_examples.output: Create delayed Vaex aggregations, execute them together, reuse cached results, and materialize only expressions that are repeatedly expensive.

output_examples.input: Prepare a large classification dataset for model training.
output_examples.output: Encode categorical fields, scale numeric features, split training and validation data, integrate a supported model, evaluate predictions, and save pipeline state.

best_practices: Prefer HDF5 or Arrow for repeated local analysis, and retain Parquet when interoperability or compression matters.
Use lazy expressions, virtual columns, selections, and delayed execution before materializing data.
Confirm paths, credentials, network exposure, and destructive actions before running remote or file-changing workflows.
anti_patterns: Converting an entire large Vaex DataFrame to pandas for routine analysis.
Binding a Vaex Server to all interfaces without authentication, TLS, and network controls.
Embedding secrets in code or deleting source files before verifying archived outputs.

faq.question: What dataset sizes does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets tabular datasets that challenge available memory, including gigabyte, terabyte, and billion-row workloads.

faq.question: Which file formats are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover HDF5, Apache Arrow, Parquet, CSV, FITS, pandas, NumPy, cloud storage, and database workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill execute Vaex code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for an agent to adapt within the user's environment.

faq.question: Can it help with machine learning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers preprocessing, feature engineering, clustering, model integrations, evaluation, state saving, and deployment patterns.

faq.question: Can it replace pandas?
faq.answer: It complements pandas when data exceeds memory or lazy execution matters. Small in-memory workflows may remain simpler in pandas.

faq.question: How should remote credentials and servers be handled?
faq.answer: Use secret managers or credential providers, prefer encrypted connections, restrict network exposure, and confirm destructive actions before execution.
